pl-l3d12c3-d1e117.summary: Notes that some ask, though curiously, whether God could have assumed human nature in the female sex.

pl-l3d12c3-d1e120.summary: Reports that some think he could have assumed a human in the female sex as he did in the male, but it was more opportune and fitting that he be born of a woman and assume a man, so that the liberation of both sexes would be shown.
claims: Some hold God could have assumed a woman.
Assuming a man born of a woman shows the liberation of both sexes.

pl-l3d12c3-d1e123.summary: Cites Augustine, 83 Questions: man's liberation had to appear in both sexes; since it was fitting to take a man, the more honorable sex, the liberation of the female sex appeared in that man's being born of a woman. So the Wisdom of God, the only Son, showed man's liberation by assuming a man in and from the Virgin's womb.
claims: Christ took the male sex as more honorable.
Women's liberation is shown in Christ's birth from a woman.

pl-l3d12c3.summary: Asks, though curiously, whether God could have assumed human nature in the female sex. Some think he could, but it was more fitting that he be born of a woman and assume a man, so that the liberation of both sexes would be shown, as Augustine explains: he took the more honorable male sex, and the female's liberation appeared in his being born of a woman.
claims: God could perhaps have assumed the female sex.
It was more fitting to assume a man born of a woman, showing the liberation of both sexes.
